basePrompt: Create an original piloted combat mech in Heavy Rig’s grounded Western military science-fiction setting. Use the selected chassis’s proportions. Give its armor weight, its joints room to turn and each weapon a visible connection to its hardpoint.
baselineStylePrompt:
ARMOR AND COLOR AT GAMEPLAY SIZE

Build the silhouette from a few recognizable masses. Give the cockpit, weapon housings and legs distinct profiles when viewed from above and in three-quarter view. Shape each armor shell with broad planar faces and a few deliberate bevels. Leave room to see where a limb meets its pivot and where a weapon ends.

Choose a compact chassis palette. Carry the main paint color across large uninterrupted armor faces, group a second color on a few whole panels or housings, and recess the joints and weapon openings into a darker value. Use a small bright visor as a focal point. Let a change of plane catch one broad highlight. The face of a launcher can show its grouped openings while its sides stay quiet.

At the size of the mechs in the attached Practice range view, the cockpit, stance and fitted weapon families should still read. Omit fine panel grids, rivet rows, hairline edge wear, dense hoses and mottled metal textures that would break into speckles. Render a clean, full-resolution 3D concept with continuous edges. Pixelation happens in the game.
presentationPrompt:
PRESENTATION FOR IMAGE-TO-3D GENERATION

Exactly one complete mech, full-body front three-quarter view, rotated approximately 35–45 degrees from the camera. Neutral standing pose, orthographic or minimal-perspective projection, camera approximately at torso height.

Both legs and feet are completely visible. Arms, weapons, and mechanical connections have clear silhouettes and sufficient separation to identify their geometry.

Clean hard-surface 3D asset reference with clearly visible armor planes and articulation.

Soft uniform ambient illumination sufficient to reveal geometry. No cinematic lighting, dramatic shadows, glowing weapons, or atmospheric effects.

Center the complete machine, occupying approximately 85% of the image height. No cropped extremities, no other machines, no text, diagrams, technical specification panels, logos, or multiple views.

chassisStyle.warden: Broad compact wedge torso with a narrow horizontal protected visor; reverse-jointed legs, two lateral gun assemblies and two shoulder modules. Preserve the squat line-fighter silhouette and substantial waist bearing.
chassisStyle.kestrel: Narrow forward-projecting beak cockpit, raised rear counterweight, slender but industrial reverse-jointed legs with rear talons, and two small lateral weapon assemblies. Preserve a compact mobile silhouette; do not bulk it up into an assault chassis.
chassisStyle.maul: Broad heavily armored humanoid industrial chassis with compact protected head, forward-jointed legs, wide shoulders and two massive forearm gauntlet housings. Replace the hardware inside each gauntlet without changing the shared chassis.
chassisStyle.longbow: Tall narrow central torso, elevated compact protected cockpit, long forward-jointed load-bearing legs, one elongated left main weapon arm and a right offhand assembly. Preserve the prominent rear cooling pack. A has an unarmed offhand; B/C replace it with a braced compact secondary mount.
chassisStyle.morrow: Low central cockpit bridge below two large outboard pod housings, broad stable reverse-jointed legs, and no humanoid weapon arms. Preserve the carrier silhouette when pod internals become energy assemblies; do not turn it into a humanoid robot.
chassisStyle.rook: Compact forward cockpit, narrow waist, forward-jointed legs, two underslung weapon arms and one central dorsal compact pod. Preserve the distinct medium raider silhouette and the same torso, pelvis and legs across A/B/C.
